rv.q: The whole thing oozes style and wit.
For sheer blissful froth, it sure gave me goosebumps.

This is a tap extravaganza to top all others, with a huge cast, many of whom were playing several different characters and, under the direction of Kathleen Marshall (also the choreographer), everyone performed some very intricate dances to absolute perfection.
Top Hat is pure escapism; dazzle, elegance and vintage Hollywood glamour in this revival of a classic musical.

Peter McKintosh’s set is an art deco delight (they really should sell some of those props as merch) and he’s also wowing us with Yvonne Milnes, delivering a dizzying array of fabulous 1930s costumes for the principals, the cameos and the ensemble, dancing girls and all.
Marshall’s choreography is never less than polished, as you’d expect.
Even Marshall's effervescent choreography struggles to energise the creaky, convoluted book.
As a night of summer entertainment however, there’s plenty here to be commended.
Overall Top Hat continues Chichester’s tradition of excellent summer musicals and is a total tonic.
Chichester Festival Theatre bring all the romance and fun of the original story to life in a magical adaptation.
It’s endearing, thoroughly enjoyable, and offers a delightful dose of Hollywood-esque nostalgia.
You can’t beat a classic, and Top Hat is feelgood theatre at its best.

cn.t: Critics find this Irving Berlin musical delivers spectacular dancing and old Hollywood glamour, though the thin, old-fashioned plot struggles to match the dazzle of Kathleen Marshall's choreography and production values.
